prompt: Override equals, hashCode and toString on ColoredBadge so the equals contract still holds across the hierarchy: a plain Badge and a ColoredBadge must never be equal in either direction.
explanation: Because the provided Badge compares with getClass() rather than instanceof, a superclass instance and a subclass instance are automatically unequal both ways, which is exactly the symmetry the contract demands. Calling super.equals first reuses that class check plus the id comparison, leaving the subclass to compare only the field it added. hashCode must move with equals, so folding the inherited hash together with the colour keeps equal badges in the same HashSet bucket.
hints: Start equals with 'if (!super.equals(other)) return false;' -- that already settles null, the class check and the id.
After super.equals succeeds you know the object really is a ColoredBadge, so the cast is safe.
Objects.hash(super.hashCode(), color) combines the inherited hash with the new field.
